events.name: Cyclone Arnab
events.window_source: IMD press release No. 5 (docs/imd_bulletins/20261027_0300UTC_press_release_27Oct.pdf, issued 1400 IST 27 Oct) and No. 6 (docs/imd_bulletins/20261028_0300UTC_press_release_28Oct.pdf, issued 1430 IST 28 Oct). START 24 Oct: the observed-track chart in both releases labels the first track point '24/12, 25KT, D' (depression, 24 Oct 1200 UTC); the 27 Oct text starts with 'cyclonic storm "Arnab"' on 26 Oct. END 28 Oct: the bulletins in the folder give no observed end (no 'weakened into a depression' observation), only forecasts: No. 6 forecasts a 'Well Marked Low Pressure Area' by 29.10.26/1730 IST, and 'crossed ... coasts ... during 0200 - 0800 hours IST today, the 28th October' with 'the landfall process completed ... by 0800 hrs IST'. So end = 28 Oct, the date of the last bulletin in docs/imd_bulletins/ (not an IMD-stated end). Only the two press releases were read in full for this window; the other 13 files in the folder are same-period bulletins and advisories dated 27 Oct 1200 UTC to 28 Oct 0300 UTC. aftermath_days 45 = the old monitor_days (45) of data/events/arnab-2026.json, counted from the end date (end = landfall day).
events.description: Cyclone Arnab reached Andhra Pradesh as a very severe cyclonic storm. IMD says it crossed the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, near 16.45 N 81.9 E, during 0200 to 0800 hours IST on 28 October 2026, with maximum sustained wind 125 to 135 km/h gusting to 150 km/h (IMD press release 6, 28 Oct). NISAR looked at the sea on 27 Oct and at the Godavari delta coast on 28 Oct, then again on 8 and 9 Nov.
cannot_tell: Radar does not measure wind speed in km/h. The wind numbers here are IMD's, not derived from the satellite.
The 'wet or flooded crops' class is weak: it cannot be told apart from normal change in fields, so it is not a public finding (docs/METHODS.md).
There is no ground truth: no field survey, tide gauge or flood map was compared with the radar result.
The 9 Nov coast picture mixes Cyclone Arnab, Cyclone Murasu (1 to 3 Nov) and the Godavari river peak (about 2 Nov). Radar cannot separate them.
Radar cannot say how deep the water was, how long it stayed, or whether homes or crops were damaged.
The 4 and 16 Oct coast scenes and the 15 Oct sea scene used as the 'normal' reference are PROVISIONAL products.
The sea difference map (27 Oct minus 15 Oct) may include a calibration offset from the provisional reference scene, so read its pattern, not its level.
The eye is faint in the radar picture and sits about 10 km from the IMD fix.
The landfall time is not settled: IMD gives a window (0200 to 0800 IST, 28 Oct), so the time stays empty here.
No S-band scene has been processed yet; every result is from L-band only.

confounders.name: Cyclone Murasu
confounders.limit_text: Cyclone Murasu (1-3 Nov) and the river peak
confounders.text: Cyclone Murasu (1 to 3 Nov) probably also put water on the land. The Godavari river peak (about 2 Nov) probably did too. This radar picture shows all of it together, not Cyclone Arnab alone.
confounders.note: Human-written. affects_dates lists the radar scene dates the note applies to; add a date when a later scene is still affected.

story.landfall_caption: Landfall point on the map: near 16.45 N, 81.9 E (Narasapuram and Razole area). IMD gives a window of 02:00 to 08:00 IST on 28 October.
story.eye_profile: The calm eye was about {eye} km from centre to edge, give or take {eye_err} km. The roughest sea was about {peak} km from the centre of the eye. Radar sees how rough the sea is. It does not measure wind speed in km/h. The wind numbers come from IMD, not from the satellite. The eye is small and weak in this radar view (about 5 km core, bright ring near 14 km).
story.before_after: Cyclone Arnab crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast on 28 October 2026, in a window IMD gives as 02:00 to 08:00 IST. A radar satellite called NISAR looked at the land before and after. It shows where the land was probably under water. The left side is the coast on {before}. The right side is the newest radar pass, on {after}.
story.murasu_caveat: Cyclone Murasu (1 to 3 Nov) probably also put water on the land. The Godavari river peak (about 2 Nov) probably did too. This radar picture shows all of it together, not Cyclone Arnab alone.
story.wind: About 125 to 135 km/h wind near landfall, with gusts to about 150 km/h (IMD).
story.sea_caveat: The brightness-rise chart compares 27 Oct with a provisional calm scene (15 Oct) that has dark patches, so read its shape, not its level.
story.case_start: On {date}, the NISAR radar satellite (a NASA and ISRO mission) passed over the Bay of Bengal. This was hours before {name} reached land near Narsapur. Clouds hid the storm from normal cameras. Radar can see through cloud, so it caught the eye of the storm.
